quotes.text: # Accept a payment using Kakao Pay in South Korea
Learn how to accept payments from Kakao Pay users.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Kakao Pay isn’t available in Singapore.
The minimum amount accepted is 100 KRW.
Additionally, you must provide the buyer’s [email address]
Stripe sends a [payment_intent.succeeded](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md#event_types-payment_intent.succeeded) event when the payment completes.

findings: The entire November base capture is a 14-line route index naming Checkout and Direct API variants; it has no amounts, supported countries, email or processor requirements, API fields, test states or payment outcomes (new raw lines 5-14). The old 310-line capture provided both variant bodies (old raw lines 8-310). The diff removes detailed body text into linked variants, a navigation-format delta with no established payment-rule change (diff lines 1-312).

The older Checkout path allowed dynamic payment methods to surface eligible methods automatically; otherwise its manually configured Session includes kakao_pay, all line items in KRW, and a buyer email, with payment/setup/subscription mode support listed (old raw lines 12-51). Hosted and embedded Session examples differ in success_url versus return_url/ui_mode; a created Session or return is not a paid outcome (old raw lines 53-103). The summary lines 17-29 cover much of this but should qualify that explicit method listing is the manual path.

The old Direct API path created a server-side KRW PaymentIntent with payment_method_types kakao_pay and payment_method_data.billing_details.email, then passed its client secret to Stripe.js for client-side confirmPayment with a return_url and local NICEPAY/Kakao authorization (old raw lines 114-161, 230-283). Secret API key stays server-side, publishable key and client secret stay in the client route; client-secret delivery is not payment success. The summary lines 31-37 represent this dated route but should not imply November reconfirmed it.

The older guide states 27 supported business locations excluding Singapore, a 100 KRW minimum, 2,000,000 KRW stored-value top-up maximum but no card-passthrough maximum, and NICEPAY identity/terms disclosure for the checkout page (old raw lines 18-41, 230-235). This supports the source's scope (source lines 13-22), but the November index establishes none of those details; preserve May attribution. The related Korea concept at wiki/concepts/stripe-korea-payment-methods.md:112-119 retains the same overview.

Old sandbox redirect testing transitions a PaymentIntent from requires_action to succeeded on authorization or to requires_payment_method on failure, while payment_intent.succeeded webhook is the post-payment event for fulfillment; the guide warns against relying on client callback (old raw lines 106-108, 290-299). The source lines 29, 37 should keep test-only versus live outcome qualification. A browser return_url carrying payment_intent and payment_intent_client_secret still requires status verification (old raw lines 283-296).

The old Direct API error branch references result.error.message although the variable captured from confirmPayment is error, so its displayed-error snippet is inconsistent (old raw lines 263-279). Treat it as a dated example defect rather than an instruction to copy verbatim or a demonstrated Stripe API change; November index has no replacement snippet.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the May 8, 2026 source ingestion and complete older raw provenance, with Checkout and Direct API parameters, country/amount conditions and NICEPAY disclosure dated to that capture; add the November 7 index as navigation only (source lines 4-7, 46-48; old raw lines 8-310; new raw lines 9-14).

Preserve the old direct server/client split, webhook finality and PaymentIntent test-state transitions with May attribution; neither November variant link proves current SDK behavior, client return status or live payment completion (old raw lines 135-161, 230-299; new raw lines 13-14).

Retain setup/subscription mode listings as old Checkout compatibility claims, distinct from this one-time acceptance procedure and the separate recurring guide in wiki/concepts/stripe-korea-payment-methods.md:81-88 (old raw lines 32-36).
unresolved_questions: The linked November Checkout and Direct API variant bodies were not pinned or read, so whether their current field requirements, UI behavior or test outcomes differ from the May combined guide remains unresolved (new raw lines 13-14).

The older Checkout prose requires buyer email but its two shown Session snippets do not include an email field (old raw lines 47-51, 55-103). The pinned packet does not establish the exact email-provision field for every Checkout integration; do not infer the requirement was removed from the examples.

findings: Add November 14-line base raw as a route-index reference while keeping May 310-line raw and the existing dated detailed summary (source lines 4-7, 13-48; new raw lines 9-14).
Qualify Checkout explicit payment_method_types as the older manual-configuration path, while dynamic methods may surface Kakao Pay automatically (old raw lines 12-16, 43-51; source lines 26-29).

Keep NICEPAY, buyer email, amount/country limits and Direct API server/client and webhook instructions dated to old variants, since November provides only links (old raw lines 18-51, 135-161, 230-299; new raw lines 13-14).
Scope the old sandbox PaymentIntent outcomes and avoid treating return_url or client callback as payment success (old raw lines 106-108, 283-299; source lines 29, 36-37).
source_assessments.reason: The captured November change is a two-variant navigation index, so raw-reference provenance and explicit historical scope are warranted; no new functional claim replaces the May guide.

answers.Q1: The complete November capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/kakao-pay/accept-a-payment establishes only two current route links, Checkout and Direct API, in new raw lines 5-14; it does not restate requirements or demonstrate a transaction. The May guide in old raw lines 8-108 and 110-310 describes South Korea customers redirected through NICEPAY/Kakao Pay, 27 merchant countries excluding Singapore, KRW, 100 KRW minimum, stored-value top-up limit, buyer email and NICEPAY disclosure. Checkout's explicit kakao_pay list is for manual configuration, while dynamic methods may surface it automatically. The Direct API creates a PaymentIntent server-side with email, passes only a client secret to Stripe.js, and confirms with a return_url; succeeded PaymentIntent or payment_intent.succeeded webhook is the payment boundary. source-stripe-kakao-pay-accept-payment.md captures much of that older route detail but should retain May attribution when November index provenance is added.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/kakao-pay/accept-a-payment, replacing the combined May guide with a November Checkout/Direct API index is navigation and presentation, not proof that a requirement or mode ended (old raw lines 8-310; new raw lines 9-14). No substantive raw delta or reciprocal policy conflict is established. source-stripe-kakao-pay-accept-payment.md must keep May country, KRW, buyer-email, NICEPAY, mode and test claims dated; the linked November variants were not read. The old Checkout samples omit an email field despite prose requiring buyer email, so do not invent a universal field from those snippets. Secret-key PaymentIntent creation belongs server-side; browser confirmation uses a publishable key and client secret. A Session, redirect, return_url query parameters or client callback is not a paid outcome: check PaymentIntent status and handle the succeeded webhook, with sandbox authorize/fail transitions scoped to tests.
